answer: Shared-resource fingerprinting.** Each identity gets a distinct slice of a common pool—compute in an orchard, bandwidth in a harbor, storage on a terrace—but its allocation pattern is derived from a seed tied to its registration history. Duplicates that reuse the same seed collide on the same slice signatures, so the collision surfaces as resource contention the operator cannot mask without re-deriving fresh seeds. That forces an attacker to pay full per-identity provisioning cost and forfeit any reuse, since every clone must occupy separate slices with no overlapping fingerprints.
